stories.title: Hindu community celebrates Diwali at home in twin cities as Krishna Temple remains closed
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Hindu community in Islamabad and Rawalpindi celebrated Diwali at their homes on Sunday instead of temples, as the only functional temple in the twin cities - Krishna Mandir in Saddar - remained closed for reconstruction.

Pakistan Hindu Sikh Social Welfare Council President Sardar Hira Lal told Dawn that Diwali had been celebrated with simplicity for the second time in the past two years because the temple remained closed and the community had no other place to offer mass prayers.

stories.title: Bangladesh's external debt increases almost threefold in decade
summary: Bangladesh’s foreign debt has almost tripled in 10 years, a steeper rise than in any other South Asian country except the Maldives, according to the World Bank.
Even so, the country has a lower debt burden relative to export earnings than Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.
External debt stands at 210pc of Bangladesh’s annual exports, more than twice what the country earns each year from foreign trade and other income.

stories.title: Iqbal and the Pakistani dream: fact or fiction?
summary: For starters, separate statehood was not floated by Iqbal first: right-wing activist Murtaza Ahmad Khan Maikash wrote it up in a four-part-series in Lahore’s daily Inqilab in 1928, premised on the same four provinces that make up Pakistan today.

While Rahmat Ali and the angry young men of Cambridge were calling for a Pakistan that stood severed, the Round Tablers—Iqbal, Jinnah, and Zafrulla Khan—wanted Muslim security inside a federal India, secured by strong provinces and a weak centre.
That’s why, at least up to 1934, Iqbal kept a safe distance from ‘the scheme of Pakistan’.

summary: LAHORE: Train services on the Lahore-Faisalabad route are all set to be restored from Nov 15, as the Pakistan Railways (PR) engineering teams have almost completed work on the restoration of a railway bridge, which collapsed due to floods in August near Sheikhupura.

stories.title: Bumpy road to export-led growth
summary: According to the World Bank’s 1993 study, The East Asian Miracle, countries such as South Korea and Taiwan combined export expansion with industrial investment, technological upgrading and productivity growth.

Unlike East Asian economies, which linked industrial support to productivity and export performance, Pakistan has continued to protect established industries without consistently requiring technological advancement or international competitiveness.

Unless industrial policy and investment incentives are linked to measurable improvements in productivity, domestic value addition, technological upgrading and export performance, ambitious targets may continue to outpace the economy’s capacity to deliver.

stories.title: Historical gurdwara on Lahore's Temple Road reopens first time since Partition
summary: LAHORE: The historical Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib on Temple Road, Mozang, which had been closed since the Partition, was reopened here on Sunday after completion of its restoration.
The gurdwara is associated with the visit of Guru Hargobind Sahib to Lahore.

According to Sikh historical accounts, Guru Hargobind Sahib accepted an invitation from the local Sikh congregation (Sangat) and stayed for three days at the residence of Bhai Jiwan, a devotee, in Mozang area which was on the outskirts of Lahore.

stories.title: Hitler’s ‘retreat’ sparks debate over Germany’s past and present
summary: PERCHED on a ridge high in the German Alps lie the burned-out ruins of a mountain house frequented by Adolf Hitler, which is now at the heart of an intense debate about Germany’s Nazi past.
But after it was gutted in a suspected arson attack last month, some believe it is time for the site to be completely destroyed, so it can shed the mantle of its Nazi past, BBC News reported.
But others want the site to become a centre of responsibility, actively confronting the Nazi past.

summary: WHEN COP31 opens in Antalya today, governments will have to show that years of climate negotiations have produced more than ambitious targets and promises of financial help.

By joining forces with other vulnerable countries, Pakistan could strengthen calls for better glacier monitoring, flood protection, and affordable climate technology.

stories.title: Climate change leads to early cotton sowing in Sindh
summary: LAHORE: In a significant shift driven by changing climatic patterns, cotton sowing has begun for the first time during the second week of November in several coastal areas of Sindh, marking a major departure from traditional agricultural practices.

Traditionally, Pakistan had two distinct cotton-growing zones: the coastal districts of Sindh, where sowing began in February and March, and the rest of the country, where planting took place from May 1 to the first week of June.

However, reports indicate that favourable temperatures during the second week of November have encouraged farmers in the coastal districts of Thatta and Sujawal, including Chuhar Jamali, Mirpur Sakro, Gharo, Buhara, Keti Bunder and Chhachh Jahan, to begin cotton sowing.

summary: LAHORE: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has increased the limit of personal loans available under the Youth Business and Agriculture Loan schemes, and reduced the minimum age limit to allow 18-year-olds to avail the scheme as well.
